name: PT Bank Central Asia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Bank Central Asia: the deposit franchise priced against its own margin
frontmatter.summary: Bank Central Asia grew loans to IDR1,063,000.0bn by September 2026 on CASA of IDR1,103,000.0bn, a 5.4% margin and 27.5% capital. This revision corrects the margin and the asset base, which cuts the target, and reads the IHSG constituent change as a flow event with no value in it. ADD on Rp5,791, a 15.4% total return.
thesis: Funding is the moat: CASA of IDR1,045,000.0bn in FY2025 and IDR1,103,000.0bn at the nine-month stage keep a 79.5% loan-to-deposit ratio and a 5.5% modelled margin [S5; S2].
Growth runs above the system: loans of IDR1,063,000.0bn grew 12.6% year on year against industry credit growth of 13.3%, and management guides 12.0% for the year [S2; S4].
Credit is not the problem the price fears: gross NPL of 1.8%, loans at risk of 4.6% and NPL coverage of 184% leave room to absorb a slower cycle [S2; S5].
Capital return is the second engine: a 72.0% payout, DPS of Rp336/share and an authorised buyback of Rp5.0tn support the 6.6% forward yield [S7; S8].

The multiple is not the case: 2.17x forward book against the 2.05x a 12.45% cost of equity warrants on a 20.8% sustainable return, so the primary method alone gives Rp4,720; the Rp5,791 target rests on residual income of Rp6,009 and a dividend discount of Rp5,791 — 15.4% total return, hence ADD [S0].

catalysts.event: Second step of Bank Indonesia's rupiah reserve-requirement cut takes effect
Full-year results and management guidance for the new book year
Annual general meeting: final dividend for the year and buyback renewal
First interim dividend decision of the new book year

blocks.text: This revision corrects the model, not the franchise, and the corrections move the target further than the flow event that prompted the note. The margin input is 5.5% rather than the FY2025 average: the third-quarter prints are 5.4% and 5.6%, and nine-month profit of IDR45,200.0bn on a book that grew 12.6% fits the lower level [S9; S10; S2]. Earning assets are now built from the funding identity — deposits plus equity plus a constant residual — rather than a fixed multiple of loans. Terminal growth moves to 4.5%, which partly offsets. FY2026E profit is IDR59,718.6bn, the run-rate rather than the old step-up. The call moves from BUY to ADD on that lower target, not on a changed view of the franchise.

The event is the exchange's removal of 296 high-shareholding-concentration stocks from the IHSG calculation from 13 November 2026, lifting BCA's weight from 9.75% to 10.38% [S20]. It changes who must hold the shares, not what they are worth; no method takes the index weight as an input. The close we hold is Rp5,325 on 11 November, before the announcement on the evening of 12 November, so the market's reaction cannot be in that price.

The operating record stands. Loans reached IDR993,000.0bn at the end of FY2025 and IDR1,063,000.0bn nine months later; funds of IDR1,301,000.0bn were funded by CASA of IDR1,103,000.0bn, and the loan-to-deposit ratio rises to 81.7% on our forecasts [S5; S2; S9; S0]. Capital was 27.5%, gross NPL 1.8%, loans at risk 4.6%, coverage 184% [S9; S2; S5]. I rate the shares ADD with a Rp5,791 target, 15.4% from Rp5,325.

The shares trade at 10.9x earnings and 2.2x book with a 6.6% forward yield. Justified P/BV, the primary method, gives Rp4,720, about a tenth below the Rp5,325 price: the market pays 2.2x forward book where a 12.45% cost of equity on a 20.8% sustainable return warrants 2.05x. The blend of Rp5,321 is at fair value, so the call rests on the other two: residual income at Rp6,009 and the dividend discount at Rp5,791, 27.3% and 22.7% above the primary, putting Rp5,631 before the scenario weighting [S0]. The reverse solve puts the price at a credit charge of -0.1%, so the market is more optimistic about credit than we are [S0] — a deliberate divergence from the house stance on Indonesian rate-sensitive lenders.

BCA is a commercial bank with four engines: consumer lending of IDR224,100.0bn, of which mortgages are IDR142,300.0bn; business lending of IDR756,500.0bn; a treasury book of government bonds and central-bank placements beyond the loan book; and fees in payments, wealth and insurance distribution [S5; S2]. At the FY2025 year-end loans were IDR993,000.0bn against funds of IDR1,249,000.0bn, with CASA of IDR1,045,000.0bn; productive lending reached IDR831,000.0bn by September 2026 [S5; S2].
Management runs a low loan-to-deposit ratio by design — 79.5% at FY2025, 81.7% on our forecasts — and we model no share shift, because it will not buy growth with price [S5; S0; S4].

Capital return links the franchise to the share price: a 72% payout, DPS of Rp336/share for FY2025, interims with IDR3,070.0bn paid in September 2026, and a buyback of up to Rp5.0tn, about the -0.80% share-count change we model [S7; S8]. Every interim is deducted from the final dividend, so the move is timing, not a higher payout [S8].
On ownership, the tradable register is a minority: the exchange-registry free float is 42.5%, and no filing tells us whether the controlling vehicles have bought or sold [S0; S20].

System credit grew 13.3% year on year in September 2026, faster than deposits, which is why the system loan-to-deposit ratio has drifted up for two years [S4]. BCA's deposits reached IDR1,301,000.0bn with CASA of IDR1,103,000.0bn [S9]. A bank funding growth from time deposits pays in margin; one whose CASA covers most of its deposits can hold price. Management lifted its corridor to 12.0% [S4].

The funding mix is where this bank differs. CASA was IDR1,045,000.0bn of IDR1,249,000.0bn at FY2025 and IDR1,103,000.0bn of IDR1,301,000.0bn nine months later, so the share rose while term deposits fell in absolute terms; current accounts grew 14.9% and savings 7.4% [S9; S10; S5]. Management describes the cost of funds as stable through three quarters [S10]. Against a house deck holding the policy rate flat at 5.8%, that is what a beta below one looks like, but no BCA deposit-rate series exists in the archive, so the beta is an assumption and the margin a calibrated constant [S10; S0].

The competitive set is the state-owned trio and the large private banks; BCA's advantage is pricing power on the liability side rather than volume [S5]. The funding franchise is the moat: a loan book can be replicated with price, a deposit franchise cannot.

Two policy levers matter. The rupiah reserve requirement was cut from 9.0% to 7.0% in two steps in November and December 2026, returning liquidity; management puts the relief at 1.0% of BCA's liquidity base, and it is in the base from FY2027E [S12]. The policy rate is projected at 5.8% for FY2027E, the ceiling for deposit repricing [S0]. Neither changes competition; both change how fast the margin moves.

The external variable is the rupiah: the house deck carries USD/IDR at 18,350 for FY2027E, real GDP growth of 5.3% and consumer inflation of 3.3% [S0]. A weaker currency raises the sovereign yield that anchors our cost of equity, and with it the multiple the market will pay — the channel through which the external balance reaches a domestic loan book.

BCA is third of the four big banks by total assets [S15]. From 13 November 2026 the exchange removed 296 high-shareholding-concentration names from the IHSG calculation, lifting BCA from 9.75% to 10.38%, the largest increase of any constituent: a passive bid changes who holds the shares rather than what they are worth, and the committee can move the weight back [S20].

Net interest income rises from IDR87,715.6bn in FY2025A to IDR90,869.3bn in FY2026E and IDR129,308.3bn by FY2030E, on loans compounding from IDR993,000.0bn to IDR1,650,585.0bn [S0]. The margin input is 5.5% in FY2026E, the mid-point of the two third-quarter prints of 5.4% and 5.6%, and 5.5% from FY2027E as the reserve-requirement cut is redeployed [S9; S10; S12]. The prints are the same quarter and we cannot resolve the difference; the range sits inside one sensitivity step, so both are shown [S9; S10].

Nine-month profit of IDR45,200.0bn grew 4.2% while loans grew 12.6% [S2]. A full year of IDR59,718.6bn leaves a fourth quarter the size of the prior year's; the earlier build required an acceleration nothing supports, and it is gone. Net interest income now compounds from the lower published margin base [S9; S10].

Earning assets are the second correction. FY2025 total assets of IDR1,586,828.5bn were funded by deposits of IDR1,249,000.0bn, parent equity of IDR281,466.5bn and a constant residual of other funding, and they stood against gross loans of IDR993,000.0bn. Holding the residual flat, with deposits growing 9.0% — a point above the 8.0% nine-month actual, flagged as a drift and carried because the CASA mix keeps the funding cost stable [S9] — and equity only by retained profit, the asset base grows slower than loans, so earning assets per unit of loans falls from 1.54x in FY2026E to 1.50x by FY2028E and 1.48x by FY2030E, while the loan-to-deposit ratio rises to 83.2% [S18; S9; S0]. A fixed ratio with a rising LDR would have overstated net interest income; the corrected path is the funding identity, not a haircut.

Non-interest income grows 6.0% a year from IDR26,604.0bn, below the FY2025 surge and above the three-year average, on 42bn transactions plus wealth and insurance distribution [S5]. Cost-to-income is held at 30.7%, because management gave no further target and the spend is committed [S5].

Provisions of IDR8,420.6bn in FY2026E are 0.8% of average loans; the derivation belongs on the page because the pack has no provisions line: reported cost-to-income of 30.7% applied to FY2025 operating income of IDR114,319.6bn gives cost, income less cost is pre-provision profit, and that less pre-tax profit of IDR71,260.9bn is the charge, which over average loans is the level held [S5; S0]. It is the LK's arithmetic, and it is flat through FY2030E, since coverage of 184% and loans at risk of 4.6% describe a book already provided for [S2; S5].

Capital is not a constraint but is no longer abundant. The ratio was 27.5% at September 2026; dividing equity by risk-weighted assets at a density of 0.97, the model lands near 27.8% and falls to 23.2% by FY2035E [S9; S0]. Return on equity is 20.5% in FY2026E against 21.1% in FY2025A; the rise to 22.0% is leverage, not franchise, since no operating input improves after FY2026E. The payout and buyback show management intends to run the buffer down, which is why residual income carries more growth than the warranted multiple [S9; S8; S0].

On earnings quality: the margin is struck on average earning assets reconciled to funding, so it is comparable with the company's print, which it was not before [S18; S0]. Fee income is the least predictable line, so we extrapolate 6.0%, not the FY2025 spike [S5]. The provisioning trend the card asks for cannot be built — no write-off series, no provisions line — so the charge is an inference from reported profit [S0; S5].

Residual income is the card's method for a bank and one of the three the engine runs: justified P/BV at 50%, residual income at 30% and dividend discount at 20% [S0]. We keep the configured weights even though the primary sits furthest below the price; re-weighting would raise the target, which is no reason. A cash-flow model is not among them: a bank's cash flow is its balance sheet, so value comes from book value, the return on it and the dividend.

The cost of equity of 12.45% is the ten-year yield of 7.4% less the sovereign default spread of 1.6%, plus an unlevered beta of 0.90 times the mature-market premium of 4.2% plus the country risk premium of 2.5%, plus a coefficient of 0.6% [S0]. The coefficient closes the gap between the engine's decomposition and the card's form — the ten-year yield plus the floor of the house rupiah band — without which the implied premium would sit under the band; we use the floor because BCA's earnings volatility is the lowest of the large banks and a wider premium would double-count the country risk already in it [S0].

Justified P/BV is primary. With a sustainable return on equity of 20.8%, a cost of equity of 12.45% and terminal growth of 4.5%, the warranted multiple is 2.0x on September 2026 book value, giving Rp4,720 [S0]. The market pays 2.2x forward book: fair value or a shade above.

Residual income capitalises the excess return year by year and adds a terminal value, giving Rp6,009, 27.3% above justified P/BV [S0]. The divergence is expected: the multiple capitalises one flat return, while residual income compounds the return the forecast earns, rising to 22.0% on the leverage path. A reader who thinks the ratio is held should weight residual income down and the multiple up. The dividend discount gives Rp5,791, 22.7% above the multiple on our DPS path from Rp352 [S0].

The re-rating leg is the one we do not carry. The pack's four-year mean book multiple is far above today's 2.17x and a return to it would be worth more than this target, but the engine produces no value at a typed multiple, so we price the idea through the discount rate: a point off the cost of equity is worth Rp8,264 in the bull. It is not base because the multiple rests on a sovereign yield that has not fallen. A reader who disagrees should own the bull [S0].

Blending the three at the configured weights gives Rp5,321 of value today and Rp5,631 on a twelve-month basis before the scenario weighting [S0]. The peers table compares the multiple with the domestic set, which we do not anchor on [S0].

The reverse solve runs on justified P/BV and says the price is consistent with a credit charge of -0.1% in FY2027E against our 0.8% — a release rather than a charge [S0]: on this method the market is more optimistic about credit than we are. The loans-at-risk trend of 4.6% against 4.8% is why we do not follow it, but the gap could equally close through a lower discount rate, in which case the price is what our cost of equity warrants.

The sensitivity grid prices what the text cannot: a wider margin and a lower credit charge lift value, and a point either way on the cost of equity moves it more than either; both margin prints sit inside one step [S9; S10; S0]. What the update changed is the target and the call. Version one of this note, published on 7 November, carried a target of six thousand one hundred and ninety-two rupiah, a total return of about twenty-eight per cent and a BUY; today's is Rp5,791 on a 15.4% total return, an ADD, about six and a half per cent lower. The published figures are spelled out rather than typed because the house rule reserves digits for engine-resolved placeholders, and the engine carries the current model only. The cut is model work, not the index event: in rupiah, the margin correction to 5.5% takes out about two hundred and twenty-seven, the funding-identity rebuild of earning assets about three hundred and fifty-three, and the terminal-growth move to 4.5% adds back about one hundred and eighty-four — a net of about three hundred and ninety-seven, of which the as-of roll contributes only a few rupiah and is kept separate from the model cut. The margin and asset inputs are sourced to the quarter's prints [S9; S10] and to the funding identity [S18]; the growth parameter is the reviewed 4.5% cap path, not a response to the price. Nothing in that chain reads the index weight, so the flow event moved no part of the target.

The scenario set assigns 25% to the bear, 50% to the base and 25% to the bull, and shocks four drivers in mirror image: the margin, the credit charge, fee growth and the cost of equity [S0]. The margin shock is the card's full pass-through — a complete repricing of the deposit base at a beta of one; the fee shock takes growth to the three-year average; the cost-of-equity shock is a point, the outer sensitivity step, the multiple leg, because in a bank the multiple is the discount rate rearranged. The bear values the shares at Rp3,640, the base at Rp5,631 and the bull at Rp8,264. No volume shock: with earning assets built from funding, a loan-growth shock without a matching deposit shock breaks the balance-sheet identity, and a stalled book's earnings effect rides the credit and fee legs. No payout shock, though a capital-stress bear with a cut payout is an asymmetry worth naming.

The shocks are equal and opposite, the base carries half the mass, and the values order bear, base, bull [S0]. The outcome is convex: the bull sits further above the base than the bear below it, because a lower charge and discount rate compound while the bear still earns above its cost of equity. Against ourselves: the weighted target of Rp5,791 is above the base value of Rp5,631, so a reader who thinks the tails are symmetric should use the base. The base still clears the house ADD floor — Rp5,631 plus the Rp352 dividend over Rp5,325 is a double-digit return — but sits below the 15.4% of the weighted target, so part of the call is the bull, and that is the arm to test first. The risks not in the grid. **Funding competition:** deposit rates could reprice faster than the policy rate if system credit keeps growing 13.3% while deposits grow more slowly, and a full pass-through costs the margin the bear carries [S4]. **Asset quality:** loans at risk of 4.6%, NPL of 1.8% and coverage of 184% are strong, but the improvement from 4.8% is the kind of move that reverses in a slowdown, and one large default would consume a year's provisioning [S2; S5]. **Regulation:** the reserve cut is a benefit now; a tightening, or a rule penalising large low-cost deposit bases, would work the other way, and we put no probability on it without a source [S12]. **Index composition:** the same committee can take the weight back, and we carry no value for it either way, so the exposure is flow-driven volatility rather than target risk [S20]. **Absorbency:** a free float of 42.5% leaves limited natural supply, amplifying flow moves without changing value [S0]. **The drawdown:** BCA was the largest foreign net sell in the bank sell-off in the week to 19 October 2026 at Rp1.8tn [S13], small against a market capitalisation of IDR654,132.3bn and so not the cause of the fall from a high of Rp8,575 to Rp5,325; the de-rating is unexplained from our sources, and the most plausible driver is the higher cost of equity the house macro stance describes, which our own cost of equity reproduces.

Signposts: a margin below the lower of the two third-quarter prints for two consecutive quarters; loan growth below management's corridor; loans at risk back above the FY2025 level; a payout cut; a reserve-requirement reversal; or a methodology cut to the index weight. Any two together move us to the bear; the index one alone would not, because we carry no value for it.

Two register measures conflict and we use one: the vendor insider aggregate of 60.8% and the exchange free float of 42.5% sum to more than the register, which is impossible, so we use the free float for every liquidity statement and drop the vendor figure [S0]. The state holds no stake and no source discloses pledged shares or a dual-class structure, so the governance question is dividend policy rather than control [S0; S7]. On investability the test is turnover: three-month average daily value is IDR1,127.4bn, far above the house liquidity-discount threshold [S0].

The annual report was not available, and the sources carry no auditor opinion, board composition or related-party balance for the insurance and securities subsidiaries, so related-party flows cannot be quantified [S7; S8]. A gap, not a clean bill. The annual meeting approved the dividend and a buyback capped at Rp5.0tn; raising the payout and moving to quarterly interims in one year is shareholder-friendly and says no capital need be retained beyond the growth plan [S7; S8].

ESG disclosure is thin but not empty: sustainable financing reached IDR280,300.0bn by September 2026, growing faster than the book [S2]. BCA does not publish financed emissions, a gap a lender of this size should close. Socially the franchise is a payments utility, so the exposure is conduct and data risk rather than labour. BCA was not among the 296 names excluded from the IHSG on 13 November 2026, and no enforcement action is disclosed [S20; S13].

Catalysts, in date order. The second step of the reserve-requirement cut takes effect in December 2026 and tests whether the released liquidity goes into loans or placements [S12]. Full-year results in January 2027 bring guidance for the new book year: the loan corridor, the margin and the credit charge [S5]. The annual meeting in March 2027 declares the final dividend and renews the buyback, and the first interim follows [S7; S8].

Between updates we monitor the quarterly margin, CASA share, loans at risk with coverage, loan growth against the corridor, the capital and payout ratios, foreign net flow in banks, and the reserve requirement against the policy rate, which together set the funding cost [S2; S9; S13; S12]. Any request to revisit the rating will come from one of those lines, not the share price.

bear.narrative: Deposit war: with system credit still growing well above deposits, the cost of funds reprices the full pass-through on BCA's deposit base (-0.77pp of margin), the fee engine stalls toward its three-year average as transaction growth normalises, credit cost doubles as loans at risk season, and the balance-of-payments regime holds the sovereign yield higher, adding a full point to the cost of equity and so cutting the multiple the market will pay for the same return.

bull.narrative: The rupiah stabilises and the risk premium unwinds: a full point comes off the cost of equity and the multiple the same return on equity warrants expands with it, CASA keeps the cost of funds below the policy rate so the margin gains the same 0.77pp it loses in the bear, fees compound at double the base rate as transaction and wealth volumes grow, and provisioning releases as loans at risk fall.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs NIM and credit cost
12-month value vs cost of equity and terminal growth

assumptions.label: Loan growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026 uses BCA's own revised guidance of 10-12% and the 12.6% 9M-2026 run-rate; FY2027-30 decelerate toward nominal GDP plus a share gain as LDR normalises under the BI cycle (industry credit +13.26% vs deposits +8.22%).

assumptions.label: Deposit growth
assumptions.basis: DPK grew 8% and CASA 10.4% in 9M-2026; deposit growth lifts toward loan growth by FY2028 so LDR settles near 83% instead of drifting, respecting industry DPK +8.22% lagging credit +13.26%.

assumptions.label: Earning assets / loans
assumptions.basis: No source publishes an earning-asset total, so the base is total assets. It is built from funding rather than held flat: FY2025 total assets of Rp1,586.8tn are funded by deposits of Rp1,249tn, parent equity of Rp281.5tn and Rp56.4tn of other funding and liabilities; the Rp56.4tn is other funding, not an asset, and its asset-side counterpart is the non-earning balance of the sheet (prior QC Q9 label fix); earning assets are the rest (BCA's assets are almost all earning). Holding the other-funding residual at Rp56.4tn, deposits grow 9.0-10.0% and equity only by retained profit, so the asset base grows slower than the loan book (12.0% falling to 10.0%) and the ratio must fall: 1.544 in FY2026E to 1.477 in FY2030E, held at 1.46 thereafter as the residual gap to the funding identity widens slightly. Holding it at 1.598 (the old assumption) while the LDR rises from 79.5% to 83% is internally inconsistent and overstated NII by 3-7% in the out-years; this path is the funding identity, not a haircut. Total assets on the display line grow with loans and are not used for NII.

assumptions.label: Net interest margin
assumptions.basis: Anchored on the last actual print, not the FY2025 average. The pack's FY2025 net interest income over average assets is 5.78%, but the two third-quarter 2026 prints are 5.41% (S9) and 5.6% (S10) on the same quarter and we cannot resolve the difference from the sources; nine-month profit grew 4.2% on a 12.6% larger loan book (S2), which is consistent with a margin near 5.5% and inconsistent with 5.78%. We therefore carry 5.50%, the mid-point of the two prints: it is the level the last actual supports, and the margin is applied to the same average-total-asset base used to strike the FY2025 figure, so the comparison is like for like. The reserve-requirement cut from 9% to 7% (S12) is additional to the third-quarter print, which predates both steps: one percent of deposits is about Rp13.6tn, roughly Rp680bn of NII at a five percent redeployment spread, about four basis points of margin, so the input steps to 5.54% from FY2027E as the released liquidity is redeployed. Deposit beta is not measured: the archive holds no BCA deposit-rate series, CASA is 84.8% of deposits and management describes the cost of funds as stable through the first nine months (S10), against a house deck that holds BI at 5.75% flat (S0). A full 100bp pass-through at a beta of one would move margin by the deposit-to-earning-asset ratio, about 0.77pp; that is the bear case, not the base. The margin is a calibrated constant, not a function of the policy rate - the deck is context here, and the flat 5.75% path is the flat-margin case.

assumptions.label: Non-interest income growth
assumptions.basis: Fee income rose 16% in FY2025 on +17% transaction frequency but averaged about 3.8% over FY2023-25; 6% assumes fees track CASA account and wealth growth, above the three-year average and below the FY2025 spike.

assumptions.label: Cost-to-income
assumptions.basis: Cost-to-income fell to 30.74% in FY2025 from 31.47% and is held there: management gives no further efficiency target and the fee and loan build carries incremental cost in line with income.

assumptions.label: Credit cost
assumptions.basis: Derived from the reported lines, not read off a provisions line the pack does not carry. FY2025 total operating income of Rp114,319.6bn (S0) at the reported cost-to-income ratio of 30.74% (S5) implies operating cost of Rp35,142bn; pre-provision profit is therefore Rp79,178bn, and pre-provision profit less the reported PBT of Rp71,260.9bn (S0) leaves Rp7,917bn of provisions, which over average loans of Rp957,500bn is 0.83%. The 0.80% we hold is therefore the LK's own arithmetic rounded, and it is held flat because the book has improved since: LAR 4.6% from 4.8%, NPL 1.79% and NPL coverage 183.8% (S2; S5). Reconciled against the desk's other large-bank books, BCA is charged above the best of them and below the worst for a book with the lowest loan-at-risk ratio in the set; the gap is not a judgement overlay but the consequence of deriving the charge from reported PBT. The reverse solve says the price needs 0.49%, i.e. the market is more optimistic than this level, not less; we do not follow it because loans at risk plateaued rather than fell and a book growing 12.6% seasons new vintages. Carried as a data gap on the card's through-cycle test: the LK gives no write-off or provisioning series at all, so a cycle-fitted charge cannot be identified; the flat LK rate is the last actual, and the bear case, not the base, carries the cycle (prior QC Q8).

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt))

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(minority, np))

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: 72% of FY2025 net profit (DPS Rp336); BCA now pays up to three quarterly interim dividends a year, so 72% is the anchor for the dividend stream and the retention that funds a 10-12% loan book.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Buyback authorised up to Rp5tn at the 2026 AGM (S7), which at the current price is 0.79% of the 122.8bn shares; BCA has executed the programmes it authorises, so we retire the full 0.8% in FY2026 and hold the count flat after that. The third interim dividend the board may declare in 2026 (S8) changes the timing of the cash, not the total: S8 states every interim is deducted from the final dividend, so payout is unaffected and only the DDM's mid-year convention understates it slightly.

assumptions.label: RWA / loans
assumptions.basis: CAR of 27.51% at 9M-2026 against parent equity and gross loans implies risk-weighted assets near 0.97x loans; held flat, consistent with the current retail and corporate mix.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth
assumptions.basis: 4.5%, between the old unsourced 4.0% and the house cap. The binding arithmetic is capital: retention is 28% of profit at the 72% payout and the model's own terminal return on equity is about 22%, so retained profit funds roughly 6% of growth a year; the house cap for IDR names is 5.0%. We take 4.5% because a bank of this size cannot outgrow the economy (real GDP plus CPI in the house macro deck, S0) for ever, and because the terminal return is the FY2035E leverage path rather than a proven level. It is below the cap and below the retention-funded rate, so it does not assume the bank grows by issuing capital.

challenges.section: 1. Business description; 5. Investment risks; 6. Governance and ESG
challenges.challenge: The note states three times that 'the controlling shareholder does not trade' (section 1 uncited; sections 5 and 6 cite [S7]) and builds the no-overhang conclusion and the index-absorbency argument on it. The archived S7 text contains only the Rp336 FY2025 DPS, the 72% payout, the Rp5tn buyback and the Rp55 interim paid 22 Dec 2025 — no statement about the controller or any holder's trading. The pack carries insider_pct 60.814 with no source field and S0 has no archived text, so the claim is uncited end to end. An uncited load-bearing governance input is FATAL under the desk rule.
challenges.answer: Claim deleted everywhere. The uncited sentence and the :::background block that carried it are gone from section 1; sections 5 and 6 now say plainly that no filing in the archive tells us what the controlling vehicles have done, and the ownership point rests only on the exchange-registry free float in the pack [S0]. No overhang conclusion is drawn in either direction.

challenges.challenge: The lead asserts 'the reweighting is a flow event, and part of the flow is already in the price', but the note's own body says 'We cannot attribute the rise to the reweighting from the sources we hold', and the price it uses (Rp5,325, price_date 2026-11-11 in fund record and the datapack market block) is the close before the S20 article (12/11/2026 21:03 WIB) and before the 13 Nov effective date. No part of the reweighting can be in that price, so the sentence gives the reader a causal story the file cannot support.
challenges.answer: The attribution is deleted. The summary now states that the close we hold is Rp5,325 on 11 November, before the 12 November evening announcement and the 13 November effective date, so the market's reaction is unknown to us and no part of it can be in that price; the rating step is disclosed as a re-band on a pre-event close [S20].

challenges.challenge: The summary says 'the forecasts, the three valuation methods and the Rp6,198 target are unchanged'; the v1 files say otherwise. history/v1/model.json tp_final 6,191.85 (the v1 report rendered 6,192), residual_income 6,615.02 vs 6,623.34 now, ddm 6,243.59 vs 6,255.64 now, with an identical inputs block — the Rp6 move is the as-of roll. Calling an unchanged target Rp6,198 misstates the published number and hides that the model was re-run.
challenges.answer: Reconciled in full: v1 published tp_final 6,191.85 (rendered 6,192), the as-of re-run on an identical inputs block gave 6,197.59, and the model corrections in this revision take it to 5,791.41. Section 4 now attributes the Rp6 move to the as-of roll, and the change list at the top carries the target delta. The report prose cannot print the digits under the no-typed-numbers law; the figures are here [S0].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E net profit of IDR63,266.7bn is 10.0% above FY2025A's IDR57,537.3bn, but 9M-2026 profit is IDR45,200bn, +4.2% (F37/F43). That requires Q4-2026 of IDR18,066.7bn, +27.6% yoy against Q4-2025's implied IDR14,159bn. Nothing in section 3 explains the step-up: the model builds NP as ROE x book and never reconciles the 9M actual, and the note calls the forecast 'deliberately boring'. The most-likely standard asks FY+1 to reproduce the last actual's economics, not a Q4 acceleration.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is reset to the 9M run-rate: profit of 59,718.6bn against 9M-2026 of 45,200bn leaves Q4 of 14,518.6bn, the size of Q4-2025, so no step-up is required. The mechanism is the margin input moved to the Q3 prints (5.50%, 5.54% from FY2027E) and earning assets rebuilt from funding. Section 3 now states the implied fourth quarter [S2][S9][S10].

challenges.challenge: The largest sourced upside is not sized. fund record own_history carries a four-year mean P/B of 4.41x (n=4) against 2.14x on FY2026E book; 3.0x on FY2026E BVPS of 2,486 is Rp7,460, ~20% above the target. The bull scenario's COE -0.5pp is a discount-rate shock (model tp 6,438), not a multiple recovery, and the method that carries 50% weight is never shocked in any scenario. The note says the stock is 'not a premium to its own record' but never puts a number on the gap.
challenges.answer: A re-rating leg is now named in section 4: the pack's four-year mean book multiple is far above the forward multiple and a return to it would be worth more than this target; it is not the base because the market's multiple rests on a sovereign yield that has not fallen and the mean was struck in a lower-yield regime. The same idea is priced through the discount rate in the bull, which is worth 8,263.53 [S0]. The engine produces no value at the mean, so no multiple is typed into prose.

challenges.challenge: Two sourced positives are neutralised rather than valued. (a) The GWM cut from 9% to 7% gives BCA 'mendekati 1 persen' of liquidity relief (S12/F41), ~IDR13.6tn on FY2026E deposits of 1,361,410; at a 5% spread that is ~IDR680bn pre-tax, ~1% of NP, and the note uses it only as an offset to unnamed deposit competition, never as NII. (b) With CAR 27.5% and section 3 saying 'capital is not a constraint', payout is fixed at 72% to 2035; an 80% payout on the same earnings is a straightforward bull leg that no scenario tests.
challenges.answer: The GWM relief is quantified and in the base: one percent of deposits is about Rp13.6tn, roughly Rp680bn of NII at a five percent redeployment spread, about four basis points, so the margin steps to 5.54% from FY2027E [S12]. Payout stays at 72% because S8 shows every interim is deducted from the final dividend and the Rp5tn buyback is return on top, so a payout step-up is not the most likely path and no payout shock is applied [S7][S8].

challenges.challenge: No scenario tests an earnings stall, although the file contains one: 9M-2026 profit grew 4.2% to IDR45,200bn while the model assumes +10.0% for the year. All four bear shocks are margin, credit, volume and discount-rate; none holds profit flat or cuts fee growth to the three-year 3.8% average the assumptions themselves cite. If Q4 delivers the run-rate rather than the modelled step-up, FY2026E NP is ~IDR60.3tn, EPS ~491 not 518, and the DPS/RI path falls with it.
challenges.answer: The stall is no longer needed as a separate shock because the base case is now the run-rate itself: FY2026E profit of 59,718.6bn implies a fourth quarter no larger than Q4-2025, so there is no acceleration to reverse. The earnings-stall channel remains in the bear through fee growth of minus four points and a doubled credit charge [S2][S9].

challenges.challenge: Two bear channels are named and not tested. (a) Deposit beta: S4 shows system credit +13.26% against DPK +8.22%, the note concedes there is no BCA deposit-rate series, and by its own figures (deposits 1,361,410 vs earning assets 1,777,232) a full 100bp pass-through is ~0.77pp of NIM, against the 0.4pp in the bear. (b) The index bullet assigns 'a low probability' to a methodology reversal with no basis and carries no scenario for it; the bear's COE +0.5pp is half the 1.0pp step the model's own sensitivity grid prices at tp 5,365 (TR 7.8%).
challenges.answer: The bear now carries a margin shock of minus 0.77pp, the full pass-through at a beta of one, mirrored at plus 0.77pp in the bull; the COE step is plus and minus a full point, the outer sensitivity step; the index-reversal probability is deleted because no source supports a number [S4][S9][S20].

challenges.challenge: The two register measures cannot both be right: the datapack market block carries insider_pct 60.814 and free_float_pct 42.46, which sum to 103.3% of the register, and the note's reconciliation — 'the exchange-registry free float ... excludes holders above the control threshold' — is not in the pack (free_float_source reads only 'IDX registry free float via the IDX-IC mirror, 2026-11-11') and cannot be true if insiders hold 60.8%. Section 5 then uses 60.8% to argue thin absorbency while section 6 uses 42.5% to argue liquidity, and the 10.38% IHSG weight's float basis is never stated, so the 'passive bid' claim cannot be sized.
challenges.answer: The register is reconciled on one measure only: the exchange-registry free float of 42.46% is used for every liquidity and absorbency statement, and the vendor insider aggregate of 60.814% is dropped because it sums past the register with the float and no source defines it [S0]. Section 2 states that the source does not say whether the 10.38% weight is free-float adjusted, so no float inference is drawn [S20].

challenges.challenge: Section 2 says the policy rate and the GWM cut 'are inputs to our margin assumption', but fund record drivers_used = {} and nim is a single flat 0.0578 with no policy-rate or deposit-beta term; the macro deck (bi_rate 5.75 flat FY2027E-FY2029E and long-term, usd_idr 18,350, CPI 3.28, GDP 5.29) appears only in prose, and the one deck variable the house flags for this sector (bi_rate) enters only as a scenario COE add-on. The declared divergence from the house 'INDO rate-sensitive (banks NIM) AVOID' stance is therefore untestable in the model — the same gap the v1 review raised.
challenges.answer: Section 2 now states plainly that the house deck is context, not a driver: the margin is a calibrated constant, and because the deck's own policy path is flat at 5.75%, the flat-margin case is the deck case [S0][S10]. Deposit beta is stated to be unmeasured because no BCA deposit-rate series exists in the archive. The sector-stance override is escalated to the Sector Lead in the return note as required.

challenges.challenge: Earning assets are held at 1.598x gross loans in every year (assumptions ea_loans), but the LDR rises from 79.5% to 83.2% because loans grow 12%/9% against deposits 9% — if loans outgrow deposits the securities/placements share must fall, so the ratio cannot stay flat. On the model's own deposit and equity lines plus the FY2025 residual other-assets block (56.3), balance-sheet-implied assets are IDR1,721.2tn in FY2026E, IDR1,874.6tn in FY2027E and IDR2,453.6tn in FY2030E against modelled earning assets of 1,777.2/1,972.7/2,637.6 — 3.3%, 5.2% and 7.5% high — and NII = nim x earning assets inherits the whole gap (roughly 4-6% of NP by FY2027E).
challenges.answer: Earning assets are now built from funding: FY2025 total assets are deposits of 1,249tn plus parent equity of 281.5tn plus 56.4tn of other assets, and with the residual held flat the ratio falls from 1.5443 in FY2026E to 1.4771 in FY2030E, held at 1.46 [S18][S9]. The LDR and asset base now agree and the 3-7% NII overstatement is removed; the corrected path is the funding identity.

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth of 4.0% is below the house 5.0% cap (fund record terminal_growth_cap_pct IDR) and far below nominal GDP in the same deck (real 5.29% + CPI 3.28%), in a model whose cash flows are nominal IDR; the basis argues real GDP plus a savings shift and cites S4, which is the 2026 loan-growth guidance article and says nothing about long-run growth. The model's own grid: g +0.5pp gives a 12-month value of 6,438 (+6.6%), worth ~7pp of total return on its own.
challenges.answer: Terminal growth is now 4.5%, below the house cap and below the retention-funded rate: 28% retention times a terminal ROE near 22% funds about 6% of growth, and a bank of this size cannot outgrow nominal GDP for ever [S0]. The wrong S4 citation is replaced with the house deck, and the drift gate is answered in the assumption basis.

challenges.challenge: Two inputs carry no source. (a) valuation.coe_premium 0.006 in fund record has no basis field; section 4 describes it as a premium 'for the concentration of the register and the market's risk appetite after the October selling', which is a sentiment argument, and it is exactly what brings the build to 12.451% — removing it takes the implied ERP to 4.40%, below the VAL_BANKS 5.0% floor, so it is a plug, not a judgement. (b) The 5.41 vs 5.6 third-quarter margin gap is explained as 'a difference of basis rather than a second quarter' with no source that says so; S9 attributes 5.41 to the financial statements and S10 gives 5.6 with no reconciliation.
challenges.answer: The coefficient now has a construction basis: it is the gap between the engine's build at 11.85% and the card's form, the ten-year yield plus the bottom of the 5.0-6.0% band, at 12.45%; without it the implied premium is 4.4%, under the floor [S0]. The two third-quarter margin prints are presented in section 3 and the sensitivity as an unresolved range inside one grid step, not as a single point [S9][S10].

challenges.challenge: fund record is 5,854 words (5,557 after front matter) against fund rules update_words [500, 3,500] — 59% over the WARN band. Only two paragraphs (the S20 passage in section 2 and the index bullet in section 5) are new; the rest restates the v1 initiation, and the length obscures that the thesis did not move while the rating did.
challenges.answer: The report is cut to 3,500 words by the lint check, from about 5,100: the summary now leads with the model delta, section 2 keeps the index paragraph, the new risk bullet stays, and sections 1, 3 and 6 are compressed to what changed since v1 [S0][S20].

challenges.challenge: The summary says the primary method is at fair value and the call rests on the other two; justified P/BV is 4,720, about 11% below the 5,325 price. The 5,321 figure is the three-method blend, and residual income plus DDM alone blend to about 5,922.
challenges.answer: Investment summary now states that justified P/BV of Rp4,720 sits about a tenth below the Rp5,325 price, that the Rp5,321 three-method blend is what is at fair value, and that the ADD call rests on residual income of Rp6,009 and the DDM of Rp5,791, both above the primary [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 5 says at the base the total return would not clear the ADD band on this price; base TP 5,631.3 plus DPS 352.35 on 5,325 is +12.4%, above the +10.0% ADD floor.
challenges.answer: Section 5 now says the base clears the ADD floor: base value of Rp5,631 plus the Rp352 twelve-month dividend over Rp5,325 is +12.4% against the +10.0% floor, while the weighted target at +15.4% sits above the base, so part of the call is the bull [S0].

challenges.challenge: Section 3 renders the load-bearing EA correction as earning assets per unit of loans falling from 1.5x to 1.5x; the inputs are 1.598 FY2025A, 1.5443 FY2026E and 1.4771 FY2030E, so the change is invisible at one-decimal rendering.
challenges.answer: Section 3 now renders earning assets per unit of loans at two decimals: 1.54x FY2026E, 1.50x FY2028E and 1.48x FY2030E, against FY2025 assets of Rp1,586.8tn over loans of Rp993.0tn, so the fall reads year by year instead of flat [S18; S9; S0].

challenges.challenge: The 6.5% target cut from the published v1 (6,191.85) to 5,791.41 is never quantified; section 4 gives only single-digit rupiah for the as-of roll and does not state the old figure or the margin and EA contribution against the terminal-growth offset.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now sizes the move and names the cause. Holding the as-of fixed and reverting each input in turn: nim 0.0578 flat to 0.0550/0.0554 is -Rp226.8; ea_loans 1.598 flat to 1.5443 falling to 1.4771 is -Rp353.4; terminal_growth 0.040 to 0.045 is +Rp183.5; net -Rp396.7, taking the v1-input target of Rp6,188.1 at this as-of to Rp5,791.41. The published v1 target was Rp6,191.85 at the 5 November close, Rp6,197.59 on the as-of roll, so the cut is model work, not the index event [S0; S18; S9].

challenges.challenge: valuation.post_bs_review omits the HSC/IHSG reweighting announced 12 November and effective 13 November 2026 (BCA 9.75% to 10.38%) [S20] and the buyback extension to 23 October 2026 mentioned in [S12].
challenges.answer: valuation.post_bs_review now records the buyback extension to 23 October 2026 [S12] and the HSC/IHSG reweight announced 12 November and effective 13 November 2026, lifting BCA from 9.75% to 10.38% [S20], with a plain no-value-impact note and S20 added to its sources; the engine has been re-run [S20; S12].

missing_bull_case.note: Three sourced upsides are absent. (1) Re-rating: fund record own_history carries a four-year mean P/B of 4.41x (n=4) against 2.14x on FY2026E book; 3.0x on FY2026E BVPS of 2,486 is Rp7,460, ~20% above the Rp6,198 target, and no scenario tests a partial multiple recovery — the bull's COE -0.5pp (model tp 6,438) is a discount-rate shock, not a multiple one. (2) The GWM cut from 9% to 7% gives BCA 'mendekati 1 persen' of liquidity relief (S12/F41), ~IDR13.6tn on FY2026E deposits of 1,361,410; redeployed at a 5% spread that is ~IDR680bn of pre-tax income, ~1% of NP, and the note consumes the whole benefit as an offset to unnamed deposit competition. (3) With CAR 27.5% and 'capital is not a constraint' in section 3, an 80% payout step-up is never tested; payout is fixed at 72% to 2035.

missing_bear_case.note: Three downsides are untested. (1) Earnings stall: 9M-2026 net profit grew 4.2% to IDR45,200bn (F37/F43) while FY2026E is IDR63,266.7bn, +10.0%; the bear shocks credit, NIM, loans and COE and never a flat earnings year. (2) Deposit beta: system credit +13.26% vs DPK +8.22% (S4/F29) and the note concedes there is no BCA deposit-rate series; by its own numbers (deposits 1,361,410 vs earning assets 1,777,232) a full 100bp pass-through is ~0.77pp of NIM, against the 0.4pp bear. (3) The index bullet assigns 'a low probability' to a methodology reversal with no basis and carries no scenario in which the weight is taken back while the October de-rating continues; the bear's COE +0.5pp is half the 1.0pp step the model's own grid prices at tp 5,365.

assumption_realism.note: Loan growth 12.0% is well anchored (9M 12.6%, guidance 10-12% in S4; the Q4 loan build of IDR49.2tn reproduces FY2025's IDR48.6tn). The margin is not: NIM is held at 5.78% of total assets for ten years against Q3 prints of 5.41% (S9) and 5.6% (S10), and the note itself says the level is 'already above both'. The balance sheet is internally inconsistent: earning_assets are 1.598x gross loans in every year while the LDR rises from 79.5% to 83.2%, so loans outgrow deposits yet the securities/placements share never shrinks — modelled earning assets exceed deposits + equity + the FY2025 residual other-assets block by 3.3% in FY2026E, 5.2% in FY2027E and 7.5% by FY2030E, and NII inherits that overstatement. ROE rising 21.6% to 23.3% via a falling CAR is disclosed; credit for that.

evidence_and_citations.note: Verbatim trace confirmed for F2/F4/F6/F7/F8/F9/F14/F16/F21/F22/F26/F27/F28/F29/F37/F38/F39/F40/F44-F46 and for the S20 numbers (9.75% to 10.38%, 296 removed, 522 retained, decision 11 Nov, effective 13 Nov, article 12 Nov 21:03 WIB) and for S12's 9% to 7% GWM cut and 'mendekati 1 persen' relief. Deductions: 'the controlling shareholder does not trade' is cited to S7, whose archived text covers the Rp336 dividend, the 72% payout, the Rp5tn buyback and the Rp55 interim paid 22 Dec 2025 and says nothing about the controller, and section 1 cites nothing at all; S4 (2026 loan guidance) is the source given for terminal growth 4.0%, a subject it does not mention; 'a difference of basis' for 5.41 vs 5.6 is asserted, not sourced; S20 carries no date in fund record; the FY2022A-FY2025A year-end multiple series the summary relies on is not in the pack (own_history holds only mean 4.41x, n=4).

valuation_method_fit.note: All three bank methods are present and the arithmetic is clean: 0.5x4,926.31 + 0.3x6,623.34 + 0.2x6,255.64 = 5,701.28 today, x1.12451 - 373.29 = 6,037.86 forward, weighted 50/25/25 = 6,197.59. The COE of 12.451% sits exactly at the VAL_BANKS floor on the card's definition (implied ERP = 12.451% - 7.45% = 5.00%), so the band is respected — credit. But the weights are the config's (PBV 50/RI 30/DDM 20), not the card's (RI engine, warranted multiple as cross-check), and section 4 still calls them 'the card's weights'; re-weighting to RI 50/PBV 30 lifts today's value to ~6,041 and the target to ~6,420, i.e. TR ~27.6% and BUY — the weighting is rating-decisive and the note neither quantifies it nor escalates it. The 34.4% RI/primary divergence clears the 30% cross-check flag and is discussed. The -120,425.1 net-debt line is shown for an equity-valued bank and is not applied to v0 (the blend above proves it), but the note never says so.

bias_and_tone.note: The lead sentence — 'the reweighting is a flow event, and part of the flow is already in the price' — is unsupported and contradicted by section 1's own 'We cannot attribute the rise to the reweighting from the sources we hold'; the price it rests on (5,325, 11 Nov) is the close before the 12 Nov announcement and 13 Nov effective date, so no part of the reweighting can be in it. 'At 2.1x forward book the market is paying almost exactly the multiple our own cost of equity of 12.5% warrants, 2.1x' is circular: the warranted multiple is computed from the same ROE, COE and g. The step-down is a 1.6pp miss of the 25% bar and reverses on a 1.3% price fall (to 5,257) or on COE -0.5pp (model tp 6,438, TR 27.9%); a reader is entitled to that instead of a considered-sounding notch change. Credit: the note runs the bear-doubled test itself and states the reverse-solve direction correctly.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The deck numbers quoted in prose are right: bi_rate 5.75 flat through FY2029E and long-term (fund record), usd_idr 18,350, real GDP 5.29%, CPI 3.28%. But fund record drivers_used = {} — no deck variable enters the model: nim is a single flat 0.0578 with no policy-rate or deposit-beta term, so section 2's 'both are inputs to our margin assumption' is false, and the declared divergence from the house 'INDO rate-sensitive (banks NIM) AVOID' tilt cannot be tested. This survives from the v1 review and matters more in an update whose only new fact is an index event: the one variable the house deck flags for this sector (bi_rate) is still prose-only.

conservatism_audit.note: Items below the last actual, the house range or the guidance, none with a source: (1) terminal growth 4.0% against the house 5.0% cap and nominal GDP of ~8.6% (real 5.29 + CPI 3.28) in the same deck, justified by a real-growth argument in a nominal IDR model and cited to S4, which is about 2026 loan guidance; the model's own grid gives tp 6,438 at g +0.5pp. (2) dps12 = 373.29, the FY2026E DPS, although two FY2026 interims were already paid (S8/S9) and FY2027E DPS is 411.02; the 12-month forward stream is nearer 411, worth +0.7pp of TR. (3) Buyback 0.80% of shares against Rp5tn/5,325 = 0.76%. (4) Credit charge 0.800% against the note's own FY2025 derivation of 0.827% (7,917/957,500) — a small optimism, not conservatism. The mirrored shocks (+/-0.6pp credit, 0.4pp NIM, 3.0pp loans, 0.5pp COE) and the 50% base are symmetric — credit. Items (1) and (2) alone move the target by ~Rp480, i.e. through the 25% bar.

calibration.note: cov_engine qc returns no flags; ROE FY2025A actual 0.21149 vs model 0.21635 (0.49pp) is inside tolerance — credit. Two gaps. (a) FY+1 is not reconciled to the last actual: 9M-2026 NP of IDR45,200bn (+4.2%) against FY2026E IDR63,266.7bn requires Q4-2026 of IDR18,066.7bn, +27.6% yoy versus Q4-2025's implied IDR14,159bn; the model builds NP from ROE x book and never touches the 9M print. (b) The lead's 'the forecasts, the three valuation methods and the Rp6,198 target are unchanged' is false on the files: v1 tp_final 6,191.85 (rendered 6,192), RI 6,615.02 to 6,623.34, DDM 6,243.59 to 6,255.64 — a pure as-of re-run moved the target Rp6. The BUY to ADD band itself is right: 23.4% is ADD under fund record (buy_min 25.0, add_min 10.0), and v1 at 5,125 was 28.1%.

signoff.notes: Approved on the files as they stand. fund record check: engine QC blocking none, facts PASS, lint PASS at 3,499 words. Read the summary and sections 1-6 from the packet and all answered items: the five round-3 items are fixed and checkable against the model. L1: the summary now says justified P/BV 4,720 sits about a tenth below the price and the call rests on RI 6,009 and DDM 5,791, with the 5,321 blend at fair value. L2: section 5 states the base clears the ADD floor and the weighted 15.4% sits above the 5,631 base, with 12.4% reproducible from the printed 5,631 plus 352 over 5,325. L3: EA/loans rendered at two decimals, 1.54x FY2026E to 1.50x FY2028E and 1.48x FY2030E. L4: published 6,192 and the 6.5% cut stated in prose with the 227 + 353 - 184 = 397 decomposition and the 3.7 as-of roll kept separate. L5: post_bs_review carries the buyback extension [S12] and the HSC reweight 9.75% to 10.38% [S20], interim Rp3.07tn relabelled pre-balance-sheet. Q17 words-for-figures is accepted as an advisory engine-owner item per the QC ruling and is not generalised. Most-likely test: FY2026E NP 59,718.6 leaves Q4 at 14,518.6 against the prior-year implied 14,159 (+2.5%), so the 9M +4.2% run-rate is reproduced without the old step-up; scenarios are mirrored (NIM +/-0.77pp, credit cost +/-0.6pp, NOII +/-4pp, COE +/-1pp) with base 50% and no unsourced one-sided haircut. Calibration gap -0.60pp, drift gate clean. Single-name batch: comps shows the industry spread SELL to BUY, so no systematic tilt; the ADD is a disclosed desk-level divergence from the house AVOID on INDO rate-sensitive lenders, accepted here with BBRI also BUY on the desk. Non-blocking observation for the next revision: section 4 compares the 2.05x warranted multiple (on September 2026 book) with 2.2x forward book, so the multiple comparison and the rupiah gap read slightly differently; the rupiah value is the engine value and correct. Rating ADD, target Rp5,791, TR 15.4%.

bias.note: Base is the Q3 run-rate, not a haircut: margin 5.5% is the mid-point of the two sourced prints (5.41/5.6) [S9;S10]; deposit growth 9.0% vs the 8.0% 9M actual [S9] is the one optimistic drift and is disclosed; terminal growth 4.5% is under the 5.0% cap and retention-bound. Scenarios mirror margin +/-0.77pp, credit cost +/-0.6pp, fee growth +/-4pp and COE +/-1pp at 50/25/25; the larger bull value follows from compounding, not asymmetric shocks.

findings.finding: RULING for the Director on the words-for-figures question: spelling the prior-version target (six thousand one hundred and ninety-two), return (about twenty-eight per cent) and BUY in words is ACCEPTABLE in this one update because QC round-2 Q11 expressly authorised it, no engine placeholder carries a v1 figure, and the figures verify against history/v1/model.json (tp_final 6,191.85, tr_pct 28.1, rating BUY) with the decomposition matching the L4 arithmetic (226.8 + 353.4 - 183.5 = 396.7, plus a 3.7 rupiah as-of roll).
